explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Matthew says they conspired against Jesus "to put Him to death." (Matthew 27:1) Notice they don't gather to talk it over or look for the truth. They've already got the plan, and morning just gives them the daylight to start.

explanations.answer: Send Him out of the city
explanations.explanation: I can see why that one tempts you, baker, but it's not what the text says. They conspired against Jesus "to put Him to death." (Matthew 27:1) Sending somebody away is a lot smaller than that, and their plan wasn't small.
Locking someone up is a plan, baker, but it's not this one. Matthew says they conspired "to put Him to death." (Matthew 27:1) Nothing in the verse says anything about keeping Him locked away.

Close, baker, but the text says otherwise. "They bound Him, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate the governor." (Matthew 27:2) Bound means tied up, so Jesus did not go untied. Pilate was the Roman governor, the one they handed Him to.

Right, baker. The verse says, "They bound Him, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate the governor." (Matthew 27:2) So He was bound, not untied. I think that's a heavy picture, and Matthew gives it to us in just a few plain words.

Yes, baker. Matthew says Judas "was filled with remorse" when he saw that Jesus was condemned. (Matthew 27:3) Remorse is that sinking, can't-take-it-back feeling. It's the kind of feeling that follows you around like flour on a black shirt, except this one is no joke.

Not joy, baker. The text says Judas "was filled with remorse." (Matthew 27:3) A man who is happy with what he did doesn't walk the silver back to the people who paid him. He returned it, and that tells us something was weighing on him.

That's a fair guess, baker, but it's not the word Matthew uses. He says Judas "was filled with remorse." (Matthew 27:3) Remorse is sorrow over what he had done, and it's why he went back to return the thirty pieces of silver.

That's right, baker. They said, "What is that to us?" and then, "You bear the responsibility." (Matthew 27:4) Judas came to them with a confession, and they handed it right back. I think that's a cold answer to a man who just said, "I have sinned."

They don't say that, baker. Judas says he betrayed "innocent blood," and they answer, "What is that to us?" (Matthew 27:4) Then they add, "You bear the responsibility." Nobody in that room agrees with him out loud.

Pilate comes up earlier, baker, because that's where they took Jesus (Matthew 27:2). But they don't send Judas there. They say, "What is that to us?" and "You bear the responsibility." (Matthew 27:4) They just push it back onto him.

explanations.answer: He throws it into the temple
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. "Judas threw the silver into the temple and left." (Matthew 27:5) He came to hand it back, and when they wouldn't take it, he threw it down. Then he walked out and left it behind.

explanations.answer: He gives it to the poor
explanations.explanation: That would've been a very different scene, baker, but it's not what Matthew tells us. Judas "threw the silver into the temple and left." (Matthew 27:5) The text says nothing about the poor getting any of it.

explanations.answer: He hides it in his house
explanations.explanation: No hiding in this one, baker. The text says Judas "threw the silver into the temple and left." (Matthew 27:5) He wanted it gone. He didn't take any of it home.

explanations.answer: It's unlawful because it's blood money
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. They said, "It is unlawful to put this into the treasury, since it is blood money." (Matthew 27:6) Funny thing, they took the silver back without a problem. It's the treasury they were careful about.

explanations.answer: It's allowed because it's an offering
explanations.explanation: Not quite, baker. They said the opposite: "It is unlawful to put this into the treasury, since it is blood money." (Matthew 27:6) Nobody in that huddle calls it an offering. They call it blood money.

The text doesn't go that way, baker. The chief priests say, "It is unlawful to put this into the treasury, since it is blood money." (Matthew 27:6) No sacrifice is mentioned, and the answer is a flat no.

Yes, baker. Matthew says they used the money "to buy the potter's field as a burial place for foreigners." (Matthew 27:7) So the silver they wouldn't put in the treasury went to a field. It's a plain ending to a heavy little scene.
I like the creativity, baker, but sheep aren't in this verse. They bought the potter's field "as a burial place for foreigners." (Matthew 27:7) That's the plan the text gives us for the field.

A market would've been a busy place, baker, but that's not it. Matthew says they bought the potter's field "as a burial place for foreigners." (Matthew 27:7) Travelers get a mention only if you count the ones being laid to rest.

explanations.answer: The price set on Him by Israel
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. The words say, "They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price set on Him by the people of Israel." (Matthew 27:9) The silver is the price set on Jesus. It's not a gift, and it's not a fine.
Not in this one, baker. The words say the silver was "the price set on Him by the people of Israel." (Matthew 27:9) Nothing in them calls it a gift. It's a price, set on Jesus.

explanations.answer: A fine for breaking the law
explanations.explanation: A fine is a punishment for what you did, baker, but that's not what the words say. They call the silver "the price set on Him by the people of Israel." (Matthew 27:9) It's a price set on Jesus.

You've got it, baker. The prophet's words say, "they gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord had commanded me." (Matthew 27:10) That matches what the chief priests did in verse 7. Matthew points to it as what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet.

It's true, baker, even if it sounds like a twist. The words say, "they gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord had commanded me." (Matthew 27:10) So the silver does go for the potter's field. That's the same field the chief priests bought in verse 7.
